query: Do federal judges appointed by different Presidents (Trump vs. other Republican vs. Democratic) differ in their voting tendencies on immigration injunction cases? Do Trump-appointed judges tend to be more supportive of Trump administration immigration policies compared to judges appointed by other Republican or Democratic presidents?

columns.explanation: Necessary to identify the specific judge and subsequently cross-reference their appointing President.
columns.definition: The full name of the presiding federal judge who issued the decision.

columns.explanation: Directly addresses the core query comparing Trump-appointed judges with those appointed by other Republican or Democratic presidents.
columns.definition: The U.S. President who appointed the judge to the federal bench.

columns.explanation: Allows grouping of judges by political party (Democratic vs. Republican) to analyze broader voting tendencies.
columns.definition: The political party of the President who appointed the judge.

columns.explanation: Directly measures the judge's voting tendency and supportiveness toward the administration's immigration policies.
columns.definition: The judge's ruling or voting stance on the challenged immigration policy or injunction.
allowed_values: Supportive of challenge / Against administration policy
Against challenge / Supportive of administration policy
Mixed / Granted in part and denied in part

columns.explanation: Helps determine if Trump-appointed judges are specifically more supportive of Trump administration policies compared to other administrations' policies.
columns.definition: The presidential administration whose immigration policy is being challenged in the case.

columns.definition: The court's decision regarding the requested preliminary injunction or stay.
